summary: Anne Feldhaus worked in Indology and religious studies, earning a doctorate from the University of Pennsylvania after studying at Manhattanville University. In 1981, she was appointed Distinguished Foundation Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University, where she became emeritus.

Anne Hardgrove is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Carleton College and the University of Michigan before joining the University of Texas at San Antonio, where she held a post in 2000.

Anne Hopkins Aitken was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Scripps College, Stanford, Northwestern, and Oxford. She founded the Honolulu Diamond Sangha in 1959 and also established the Maui Zendo.

Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who was a graduate student at the University of Chicago in 1991. She held posts at Cornell University, Harvard University, and the Pali Text Society.

Anne MacDonald works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, having studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida, Ashok Aklujkar, Lambert Schmithausen, and Karin Preisendanz. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and Vienna.

Anne Nishimura Morse works in Japanology, history, and archaeology. She studied under John M. Rosenfield, Taka Yanagisawa, and Yutaka Hirata, and held visiting posts at Smith College, Tokyo National Research Institute, Nara National Museum, and Kyoto National Museum.

Anne Ruth Hansen works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history, having studied under Charles Hallisey. She was affiliated with the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee and has held associate professor and professor posts at the University of Wisconsin–Madison.

Anne-Marie Blondeau is a Tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein as well as traditional teachers Dagpo Rinpoche, Yonten Gyatso, and Geshe Ngawang Dakpa. She held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Anne-Marie Esnoul was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Masson-Oursel. She held posts at the CNRS, EPHE, and Institut de civilisation indienne.
Annegret Bollée was a linguist who pursued her studies at the University of Hamburg, Aix-Marseille University, and the University of Bonn.

Annemarie Schimmel studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Marburg under Hans Heinrich Schaeder and Friedrich Heiler. She held professorships at the University of Marburg, Ankara University, and Harvard University.

Annemarie von Gabain was a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin, she held posts there from 1935 to 1945 and was a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1950 to 1966.

Annette Baier was a philosopher who completed degrees at the University of Otago and Somerville College. She held faculty appointments at Carnegie Mellon University from roughly 1968 to 1973 and at the University of Pittsburgh from 1973 to 1995.

Annette L. Heitmann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Vienna, studying under Christian Lindtner and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Annette Schmiedchen is a scholar of Indology and history who earned her PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin and completed her Habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, holding posts at both institutions.

Annie Montaut is a linguist and Indologist who studied under Nicole Balbir. She held positions at Normal Higher School of Tunis, Queen's University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, Paris Nanterre University, and INALCO.

Anthony C. Yu was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago. He taught at the University of Chicago from around 1968 until 2005.

Anthony Cerulli specializes in Indology and religious studies, having completed his studies at the University of Chicago. Around 2014, he served as Director of Graduate Studies and Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a sinologist and historian who studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak. He served as lecturer in Chinese at Leiden in 1946 and as professor from 1956 to 1975.

Anthony Kennedy Warder was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at SOAS under John Brough and William Stede. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh before serving at the University of Toronto from 1963 to 1990.
